beats.narration: The stake is down. One seat is empty.
beats.headline: One seat is empty.

beats.narration: Who do you trust to fill it? This is OMERTÀ: a multiplayer mafia strategy RPG, played in your browser.
beats.headline: OMERTÀ

beats.narration: Meet Nico. One name, a little cash, no reputation. Nico's story starts with one simple question: what's worth risking?
beats.headline: One name. No reputation.
labels: Your first step into the city

beats.narration: His first job is small. The cost is nerve; success earns game cash and respect.
beats.headline: A small job. A real result.

beats.narration: Now there's a choice: train, bank some money, or risk another job. Training spends energy to improve his stats.
beats.headline: What does the next move cost?
labels:
Take a job
Spend nerve; accept risk

Choose again
Resources shape the next move

beats.narration: Even a bank deposit spends time in vulnerable transit. Progress is deciding what to put at risk next.
beats.headline: Safety has a journey time.
labels: Cash in transit can be looted

beats.narration: Eventually, Nico earns a Path. The Gun favors street combat. The Ledger builds income through fronts and trade. The Kitchen improves cook quality. The Wheel moves convoys faster. The Shadow shortens searches. The Ring improves duels and bouts.
beats.headline: Six ways to become useful.

beats.narration: Each edge brings a drawback. Nico chooses the Wheel.
beats.headline: An edge has a price.
labels:
The Wheel
Faster convoys; slower cooking

The Gun
Combat edge; weaker goods sales
beats.note: Path choice is gated by progression and cost. It does not create a required heist composition.

beats.narration: He likes routes, engines, and arriving before somebody changes their mind.
beats.headline: Nico chooses the Wheel.
labels: Build a specialty that people need

beats.narration: Mara chooses the Gun. Their Paths don't magically solve a heist; the job still checks their preparation and abilities. But they've found different reasons to log in, and different things to bring to the table.
beats.headline: Mara brings a different edge.

beats.narration: Routes connect more than places. A business earns, but upkeep and exposure eat into the plan.
beats.headline: Income takes work.
labels:
A front
Income, upkeep and exposure

A Kitchen batch
Ingredients, time and collection

A market
Goods, price and cargo limits

beats.narration: A Kitchen batch takes time. Goods occupy cargo space.
beats.headline: Production runs on a clock.
labels: Time is part of the cost

beats.narration: Cars can be repaired, sold, or broken down; boats put freight on vulnerable water.
beats.headline: The route is part of the trade.
labels:
Land freight
District pickups · trunk · convoy

Separate sea runs
Offshore contraband · boats

Movement has costs
Capacity, time and interdiction

beats.narration: A price is only useful if you can get the goods there. For Nico, transport becomes a business decision, not background scenery.
beats.headline: A price. A receipt. A trunk.
beats.note: Actual local purchase; fees make the debit differ from the spot price.

beats.narration: Around that work: races, boxing, the Den, a Speakeasy, loans, auctions, fixers. Events and NPC activity change the surroundings. The next opportunity may be across town.
beats.headline: Other reasons to return.
beats.note: Events and NPC activity change the conditions around you.

beats.narration: Nico forms a Crew: a small circle for mutual aid.
beats.headline: A Crew is a small circle.

beats.narration: A Family is a larger structure, with hierarchy, a treasury, rivals, and territory. They're different commitments.
beats.headline: A Family is a larger commitment.

beats.narration: For this heist, a temporary team fills two seats: wheelman and muscle. Nico puts up the stake.
beats.headline: One operation. Two seats.

beats.narration: Mara joins. Preparation improves the odds; it doesn't erase the risk.
beats.headline: A name fills the empty space.

beats.narration: Families contest districts and commit resources to wars. Convoys move through dangerous routes. Commission seats bring votes on specific city rules. The game can enforce a stake or a role. A promise between friends is still a promise.
beats.headline: Larger ambitions attract rivals.

beats.narration: A wreck becomes salvage. Salvage becomes material. An eligible recipe turns material into something useful, with a traceable history. That's one part of the World Graph: the city keeps connections that matter.
beats.headline: Objects carry a history.
labels:
Crafted item
Custody and provenance persist

beats.narration: In this city, knowledge has permissions. Discoveries aren't automatically shared with everyone. Two investigators can need independently obtained evidence, not two copies of one clue.
beats.headline: Knowledge has permissions.
labels:
An original discovery
Who obtained it matters

Permitted sharing
Access is checked again

Independent evidence
Copies do not create new sources

beats.narration: Advanced coordination adds contributions and approval; it isn't ordinary Crew chat.
beats.headline: A contribution is more than a promise.
beats.note: Family operations coordinate contributions and approval. Crew play has a separate role.

beats.narration: The Living World Director selects authored situations from game state.
beats.headline: An authored city can react.
labels:
Bounded outcomes
No automatic asset faucet

beats.narration: Every discovery can change the next move.
beats.headline: A discovery changes the next move.

beats.narration: Nico's neighbor might be a person. Or a program operated by one.
beats.headline: People. Programs. NPCs.
labels:
Human player
Chooses through the interface

Player-operated agent
Uses supported game interfaces

NPC
Part of the authored city

beats.narration: Here, a sample agent reads an allowed action, submits it, and receives changed game state. The result changes what happens next. An agent makes decisions through the same action-and-result loop.
beats.headline: Read. Choose. Receive the result.
labels:
Read allowed actions
Nerve 10 · game cash $500

Submit one action
Take a street job
Cost: 3 nerve

Receive game state
Nerve 7 · game cash $607
Respect 4
beats.note: Every action checks permissions, spends resources and changes what the agent can do next.

beats.narration: Supported automation has limits: permissions, resources, risk, and bounded actions. NPCs are a separate part of the city.
beats.headline: Automation keeps its boundaries.
labels:
Bounded Alpha
No PvP, borrowing or wallet actions
beats.note: Player-operated agents use supported interfaces, permissions and bounded actions.

beats.narration: To follow the money, separate three balances. Game cash pays for city life. In-game OMR buys selected equipment, access, and services; some privileges require holding or staking it. Wallet OMR lives onchain.
beats.headline: Three balances. Three boundaries.

beats.narration: The funded Window spends OMR for game cash. Cash doesn't convert back. Limited game rewards aren't automatic wallet payouts. Many spends recycle OMR; they don't destroy token supply.
beats.headline: Utility is consequential.
beats.note: Selected gear, intelligence, protection, services and access. Holding/staking gates apply. Many spends recycle inventory.

beats.narration: The market adds another layer. Trading fees fund separate developer, community, real-world asset, and liquidity budgets.
beats.headline: Trading fees have destinations.

beats.narration: Protocol-owned liquidity remains protocol-controlled. Inventory bonds sell existing OMR released over time. Liquidity rewards need qualifying positions and funded campaigns. Market rewards depend on qualification and available funding.
beats.headline: Inventory and liquidity are funded.

beats.narration: Successful arbitrage can contribute a share of realized profit to reserves. Families compete for designated trading-fee rights, not the pool's principal.
beats.headline: A fee right is not the principal.

beats.narration: Real-world assets are interests tied to assets outside the game. The system includes Stock Tokens and Commission choices.
beats.headline: Assets outside the game.
beats.note: Stock Tokens provide exposure, not ownership of company shares. Eligibility applies.

beats.narration: Allocating a fee is the first step: acquisition, custody, eligibility, and delivery each have their place. Purchase, custody and delivery follow their own rules. Holding OMR does not promise everyone a payout.
beats.headline: Allocation is only the first step.
beats.note: Asset selection follows Commission decisions and eligibility rules.

beats.narration: Back at the heist, somebody talked. The result doesn't name them. Everyone goes to jail.
beats.headline: Somebody talked.

beats.narration: A character can die; the account continues, with only specified legacy preserved. An heir doesn't recover everything. Seasons have separate rules.
beats.headline: The character ends. The account continues.
labels:
Death
Street assets and balances can be lost

Seasons
Separate reset and prestige rules
beats.note: Legacy example: prestige and remaining account OMR, after applicable loot and death duty.

beats.narration: Eligible items can be extracted. Exported gear and vehicles stop working in-game. Combat cannot seize unrelated external wallet holdings.
beats.headline: Extraction has a tradeoff.
labels:
In-game consequence
Exported assets become inert

Wallet boundary
Unrelated holdings are not combat loot
beats.note: Only eligible gear, cars and boats can be exported.

beats.narration: You can buy equipment. You cannot buy trust.
beats.headline: You cannot buy trust.

beats.narration: The next time that envelope comes round, Nico isn't just filling a seat. Someone is counting on him. From needing a favor to being worth calling.
beats.headline: Someone is counting on him.

beats.narration: Choose your path. Find your people. Make your name.
beats.headline: Make your name.

beats.narration: OMERTÀ. Who will you bring? Start playing at omerta.fun.
beats.headline: Who will you bring?
